instructions: Cut the 6 tbsp butter into small cubes and put them in the freezer for 15 minutes. Measure 3/4 cup of the milk and keep it in the fridge until you need it.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
In a large bowl, whisk together 2 cups of the flour, the 1 tbsp baking powder, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt.
Add the cold butter and cut it in with a pastry cutter or two forks until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs with some pea sized bits of butter left.
Pour in the cold milk you measured and stir with a spoon until it just comes together into a shaggy dough. Don't keep stirring once the flour is wet.
Sprinkle 1/4 cup of the flour over the counter and turn the dough out onto it. Press it together gently with your hands.
Fold the dough in half and pat it flat. Turn it a quarter turn and fold it again. Do this 5 or 6 times in all, working gently.

Pat the dough out about 1 inch thick. Cut straight down with a 2 1/2 inch cutter, without twisting, and set the biscuits on the sheet almost touching. Press the scraps together and cut again until you have 8.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the tops are just turning golden.

While they bake, put the 1 lb sausage in a large skillet over medium high heat. Cook it for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles with a spatula, until it's browned and there's no pink left. Leave the fat in the pan.
Sprinkle the last 1/4 cup flour over the sausage and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until you can't see any dry flour.
Pour in the remaining 2 1/2 cups milk slowly, stirring as you pour so no lumps form. Stir in the 1 tsp pepper.
Turn the heat down to medium and let it bubble gently for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon. It thickens a little more as it sits.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Split the warm biscuits in half, put two on each plate and spoon the gravy over them. Serve straight away.
method_notes: Both make a quick baking powder biscuit with very cold butter and milk, then brown a pound of breakfast sausage, cook flour into its fat and whisk in about 2 1/2 cups of milk until thick. Spend With Pennies (the lead) folds the biscuit dough over itself 5 or 6 times for layers, bakes at 425°F and leaves the gravy unseasoned apart from optional red pepper flakes. Natasha's uses half and half in the biscuits, adds 2 tbsp butter to the sausage pan, cooks the flour for 3 minutes and seasons the gravy with plenty of coarse black pepper. This one follows the lead's biscuits and adds the black pepper from Natasha's. The lead says 7 servings, and this serves four at two biscuits each.
